analysis: Examined all six units. (1) docs/reference/configuration.md: the only changed line is 594, a documentation note on MLX_QUANTIZED_CONSTANT_CACHE saying a bf16 GPT-OSS checkpoint keeps bf16 activations, so no widening is needed and the cache does not apply. It changes no code, no defaults and no security controls. The head text I was given starts at line 312 and does not include line 594; I confirmed the change only from the patch excerpt. Nothing in the visible text touches prefix-cache policy, TTL, HMAC lookup tags, KEK handling, attestation or authorization (T-041, T-053, T-054). (2) provider-swift/.../EngineV2Bridge.swift (hunk at 129-136): comment-only change to the kvBytesPerToken doc, which now points to EngineV2SlotFactory.slotKVBytesPerToken. No executable change. The comment reflects a possible behavior change in KV sizing (per-layer observed K/V types in place of contiguous GPT-OSS fp32 delta handling), but that logic lives in unchanged files not supplied. (3) libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule: pointer bump from 0351444e to f2eb29b8. The patch contains no submodule diff, so its contents are unreviewed. This is a supply-chain and code-review coverage gap. The submodule holds native inference, KV-cache, prefix-cache and MTP code relevant to TB-007, T-028 and T-041. The documented changes (the cache note and the new KV pricing comment) suggest KV accounting and quantized-constant behavior changes, but I cannot verify them. Integration should check the submodule diff for changes to cache isolation, at-rest encryption or memory admission. I report no finding because there is no evidence of a concrete regression. The bump is flagged for deeper review because of the unverified submodule contents.
